panels.title: Uptime, 7 d

targets.expr: 1 - (1 - avg_over_time((min(wojtus_gateway_connected{job="wojtusdiscord"}) or on () (0 * max(up{job="wojtusdiscord"})))[7d:1m])) * count_over_time((min(wojtus_gateway_connected{job="wojtusdiscord"}) or on () (0 * max(up{job="wojtusdiscord"})))[7d:1m]) / 10080

panels.description: 1 minus the time each part was seen down, as a share of the full 7 days: bot process, Discord gateway, public URL, Postgres. Green from 99.9% (10 minutes down in a week), yellow from 99%. A deploy restart counts as down time: about 15 s, 0.0025% of a week, so a few deploys a day stay green and a crash loop does not. Time before a series existed counts as up. The gateway is read once per minute: a reconnect of a few seconds counts as one minute when a sample falls inside it, and not at all when none does.

panels.description: Downtime rows written, gateway socket closes and warm reconnects per interval. Deploy and restart gaps are not counted here: the bot counts the row in the process that stops, or before its metrics are up, so no scrape sees it. The series shows only a downtime that opens while the process keeps running (gateway loss, database unreachable). For a deploy gap see the Deploy markers and the table bot_downtime_intervals. Counts include the first sample of a new series, which increase() and rate() miss: the bot creates a counter series on its first increment.
